NEWS: Elon Musk says one reason for taking SpaceX public is to let the public own a part of the company.

One of the reasons I took SpaceX public is so that the public could participate... they could own a piece of SpaceX.

Musk explained that a public listing would allow millions of people to become shareholders, whereas private companies are limited to only a few thousand shareholders.

NEWS: Google's investment in SpaceX has grown into one of its biggest wins. 🚀

• Google now owns roughly 5% of SpaceX.
• That stake is valued at nearly $94 billion.
• Google's original investment was approximately $900 million.
• The investment has grown by more than 100× in value.

A long-term bet on SpaceX has become one of the most successful strategic investments in the tech industry.

Elon Musk: “This Will Be One Of Tesla’s Best Years Ever”

In conclusion, we're super excited about our autonomy and robotics roadmap.

There's so much awesome stuff coming. It's, like I said, hard to squeeze everything into one call, but we'll have a lot of product announcements.

And this is going to be a great year for Tesla. I think it will be one of our best years ever.

And then I think next year will be even better.

So, in conclusion, I want to thank the Tesla team for their excellent execution and all of our supporters for joining us in Australia.

NEWS: Elon Musk discussed the taxes he says he pays in a new interview.

For my stock options, I pay about 45% in taxes. Then when I die, there will be another roughly 45% tax. At the end of the day, I'll have about a quarter of what I have.

Musk said his tax burden includes federal income taxes, California state taxes on the time he worked there, and potential estate taxes.

Source: @TheEconomist

Elon Musk: Tesla’s Robotaxi Goal Is Speed — But Safety Comes First

With Robotaxi, our goals are very ambitious, but we do need to be cautious about causing any accidents or causing any harm to anyone.

Although there are, I think, 30 to 40,000 automotive deaths per year in the United States alone, most of those do not generate any publicity.

You never really read about almost any of those.

But if we injure even one person, it becomes a worldwide headline news story, and regulators will immediately clamp down on all our activities.

And we don't want anyone to get hurt.

So, we are scaling Robotaxi as fast as humanly possible, but while making sure that we do not harm anyone at all.

Ideally, we don't even want to run over a pet.

So, that's really the constraint: we want to go as fast as possible, but without causing harm to anyone.

Elon Musk: Tesla’s Mega Pods Could Transform AI Computing Everywhere

We're also building out a mega pod design that has — because, for computers with x86, it's a very x86 computer with the Tesla AI computer.

You know, it's got this visual Optimus in a box, a mega pod kind of like the Megapack packaging.

So, we put a large number of four-plus x86 combos into a giant box, essentially. And these boxes can be placed anywhere in the country or outside the country.

This allows us to scale AI compute using disaggregated electricity production.

Again, there are lots of places all around the world, including Superchargers. I think we get something like seven gigawatts of power at our Superchargers.

And we can place mega pods at many of these Superchargers and have distributed power for AI.

So, I think that could be quite a big deal.

Elon Musk: Tesla’s Secret AI Chip Factory Could Change Everything 

That said, we expect to announce their location soon and provide more details about our plans in that regard, but we'll leave that to the product launch announcement.

Rather than trying to squeeze it into an earnings call, I think this is a very big announcement and deserves to have its own spotlight, instead of being squeezed into an earnings call.

But I do think this is going to be an amazing initiative, and a necessary one. Without it, we will be constrained in our ability to scale up mass production because we simply won't have enough AI chips.

So, it's crucial to solve that.

And we'll have to solve memory, logic, and packaging in order to scale.

We'll leave the rest for its own announcement.

We've placed equipment orders for our development fab in Austin. And that development fab, I think, is pretty cool because it's intended to have lithography mask production, logic, memory, packaging, and chip testing — all under one roof.

So you can have a very fast iterative cycle, try out new chip designs very quickly, and see if they work.

I don't think such a building exists anywhere on Earth.

So this is really going to be super helpful as we try some exciting, adventurous, high-risk, high-payoff bets.
